after.title: Unbounded error time space counting model
after.statement_or_definition: Use fixed multitape fair-bit probabilistic machines with read-only uncharged input, charged work cells, worst-case halting bounds on every branch and an explicit random-access versus sequential simulation convention. PrTIME(t) and PrTISP(t,s) mean acceptance greater than one-half on YES and at most one-half on NO with time O(t) and work space O(s). Exact ties can be normalized with an extra bounded coin gadget before complementing. For oracle A, PrTIME^A(t) charges writing query strings and supplies exact classical oracle answers. Define LCH1=PrTIME(n), LCH_(k+1)=PrTIME(n)^(LCH_k). Majority formulas use at-least-half assignments; strict versus nonstrict majority conventions require an explicit threshold adjustment.
proof_obligations: State clocked branch resource and oracle tape rules; finite fair bits give dyadic probabilities. Prove strict/nonstrict majority conversion by a biased acceptance offset smaller than the least nonzero dyadic gap and explicit extra coin bits. Root PTM definition is reused for transition semantics, not for unbounded-error time-space theorems.

after.title: Probabilistic polynomial time hierarchy
after.statement_or_definition: For rational 0<a<b with time-constructible polynomial bounds, PrTIME(n^a) is properly contained in PrTIME(n^b) in the declared uniform unbounded-error probabilistic machine model.
proof_obligations: Use the source time-hierarchy diagonalization: enumerate encoded clocked machines, simulate the selected one within n^a polylog n time, normalize its possible tie by a dyadic offset below its minimum nonzero branch probability, and complement its threshold decision by swapping accepting/rejecting outcomes with the offset gadget.

Padding permits infinitely many encodings of each fixed program and absorbs the simulation constant. The universal overhead is below n^b for large n; finite exceptions are hardcoded. Author exact clock, tie and encoding bounds rather than importing nondeterministic hierarchy as a probabilistic theorem.

after.title: Counting time space to linear hierarchy
after.statement_or_definition: For constants alpha>1 and 0<beta<1 there exists finite integer tau(alpha,beta) with PrTISP(n^alpha,n^(1−beta)) contained in LCH_tau.
proof_obligations: Clock/time-stamp configurations, of count at most2^O(n^(1−beta)); subdivide a length n^alpha path into n^beta segments and sum over checkpoint tuples, multiplying subpath counts. Repeat a ceiling number of subdivisions until segment length is bounded; round powers/segments explicitly and use zero-padding for short end segments.

This produces constant-depth arithmetic count circuits of2^O(n) gates and polynomial output bit length. Substitute the uniform arithmetic supplier. Gate adjacency has an LCH connection predicate; if only logspace multiplication uniformity is supplied, author the finite alternating/linear-counting evaluation of its polynomial-log-length predicates. Evaluate each threshold layer by random gate guessing with unbiased off-fanin branches and exact majority threshold adjustment, giving finite tau. Every simulation/table/bit bound is local authoring work.

after.title: Tight majority formula completeness
after.statement_or_definition: Every LCH1 language reduces to MajSAT, and every LCH2 language reduces to MajMajSAT, with output length n log^O(1)n and each output bit computable in log^O(1)n time and O(log n) space, in the stated input/machine/formula encodings.
proof_obligations: For LCH2 first collapse adaptive oracle calls into one final query using a unique witness for the accepting-path rank at the one-half threshold, as Section3.2 does. Author the exact C=TIME conjunction and rank sign-testing construction with linear resource bounds; generic PP closure alone does not supply those bounds.

Obliviously simulate the linear-time computation with n log n time, encode its deterministic trace by a unique-witness formula of n polylog n size, and use the source auxiliary-selector variable to center counts at exactly half. Apply this inside the outer majority for the two-block formula. Provide actual bit-index generation and logarithmic workspace for the reduction; their uniformity, uniqueness, threshold and length proofs cannot be replaced by ordinary polynomial NP completeness.

after.title: Unbounded error counting time space alternative
after.statement_or_definition: For every real d and epsilon>0 there exists c>1 such that either MajMajSAT is not in PrTIME(n^c), or MajSAT is not in PrTISP(n^d,n^(1−epsilon)), with exact majority and resource conventions as defined on this page.
proof_obligations: Allender Theorem4: for 0<e<1 and a>1, assuming PrTIME(n) contained in PrTISP(n^a,n^e), choose b>1 with be<1. Padding then puts PrTIME(n^b) in PrTISP(n^(ba),n^(be)), hence LCH_tau by counting speedup. If LCH2 were in PrTIME(n^c), recursive oracle padding collapses LCH_tau into PrTIME(n^(c^(tau−1))). Choose rational1<c<b^(1/(tau−1)), contradicting the polynomial hierarchy supplier; enlarge tau to≥2 if necessary.

Transfer assumed MajSAT/MajMajSAT algorithms through the tight formula reductions, shrinking epsilon and increasing d by fixed exponent slack to absorb polylog factors. Pick a>max(1,d) and 0<e<1 appropriately; choose the final c>1 below the class-level exponent so polylog reduction factors are absorbed. Larger epsilon/negative d only strengthen the denied space/time claim; handle finite lengths separately. This derives VMW Lemma1 with its exact quantifiers.

before.statement_or_definition: In the exact VMW random-access quantum-machine model defined on this page, let MajSAT ask whether at least half of assignments satisfy an input Boolean formula, and MajMajSAT ask nested at-least-half quantification over two disjoint variable blocks. For every real d and epsilon>0 there exists c>1 such that either MajMajSAT has no bounded-two-sided-error quantum algorithm of time O(n^c), or MajSAT has no such algorithm simultaneously of time O(n^d) and space O(n^(1−epsilon)). Consequently MajMajSAT has no bounded-error algorithm simultaneously of time n^(1+o(1)) and space O(n^(1−epsilon)). This established target remains on authoring/source hold until its Allender supplier is locally supplied; it is not a current enabled inference or an open problem.
